notes.analysis: Reads the evid set. Domains: legal, psychology, social work. The method folder is the skill.
notes.analysis/legal: Methods for the law and the record. The method folder is the skill.
notes.analysis/legal/credibility: Whether a statement can be relied on: contradictions, history, a recorded condition, plausibility, corroboration.
notes.analysis/psychology: Examination, opinion, the standards that governed the work, and the terms the psychologist used.
notes.analysis/psychology/examination: Who was seen, which methods the report says were used, and what it says it did not do.
notes.analysis/psychology/opinion: Each opinion next to the observation the report cites for it.
notes.analysis/psychology/professionalism: Whether the terms are the professional ones, used correctly, and explained to a lay reader.
notes.analysis/psychology/standards: Whether the psychologist was authorized, and which statute, guidelines, and diagnostic system applied.
notes.analysis/social-work: add a similar standards skill as for psychology, make sure that it tells the agent what to get and how to extract the standards without repeating standards here
notes.analysis/social-work/investigation: What was looked at, who was spoken to, and what the record is missing.
notes.analysis/social-work/measures: What was proposed or in force, and what the record says it was for. The legal test is proportionality.
notes.authoring/graphics: Pictures in a document: timeline, org net, sankey, charts.
notes.authoring/graphics/charts: A bar, a line, or a distribution, as SVG.
notes.authoring/graphics/orgnet: How organisations connect. Neato, D2, or Mermaid.
notes.authoring/graphics/sankey: A flow of quantities from one stage to the next.
notes.authoring/quotation/labquote/SKILL.md: Verbatim quotes in Typst from a Hayagriva refs.yml. Authoring, not analysis.
notes.authoring/templates/book: Typst book. Chapters are separate files included from main.typ.
notes.authoring/templates/booklet: One file. Compact title, then the text.
notes.authoring/templates/brief: Description and date on one line, then the body.
notes.authoring/templates/letter: Sender, date, recipient, and subject, then the letter.
notes.authoring/templates/plain: Centered title and an optional date.
notes.authoring/templates/quote_summary: A document that is only the relevant labquote passages. It does not conclude.
notes.authoring/typesetting/typst_use/SKILL.md: Page, body text, and title block. The document is the folder under author/templates with the same name.
notes.ingestion/council-of-europe-download/hud: A file, not a directory. No extension means the body is the raw URL of a skill that lives in another repo. Same pattern as lawcite, domdb, and did.
notes.jura: Main router skill. The directories are the workflow.
notes.jura/SKILL.md: Same file as the root SKILL.md (symlink). The repo session loads the root; jura/ is the install directory, and its name is the skill name.

feedback.quote:
# contradiction

A contradiction is two accounts of the same thing that do not match.
Those accounts may come from one speaker at different times, from different people, or from a speaker set against the documents.

The work starts by collecting assertions of fact.
An assertion is about an event, a condition, or a person's conduct.
Each assertion is copied verbatim, with its page.
Opinions, legal argument, and pleasantries stay out.

Each assertion notes who said it, which event it concerns, the date they give, and whether they affirm it or deny it.
A short neutral restatement is for grouping only.
